solution.brief: Wasp_Rule defines one directional connection; create two swapped-index rules for mutual bidirectional connections between parts.
solution.principle:
Wasp aggregation uses directional rules to control which connections can mate, requiring explicit definition of each allowed direction; part names and 0-based connection indices must precisely match their source definitions to avoid silent failures.

Related insight: Related insight: WaspRule objects produced by Wasp_Rule are required inputs to Wasp_Stochastic Aggregation — the aggregation component cannot run without both WaspPart definitions and WaspRule objects. Rules are consumed each aggregation step as the engine randomly selects which connections to grow.

intents: how do I define connection rules in Wasp
set up aggregation rules between parts
make two parts connect to each other in Wasp
why aren't my Wasp parts connecting
symptoms: parts not connecting during aggregation despite rules being set
aggregation runs but ignores certain part combinations
only one-directional connection happening when bidirectional expected
rule output shows unexpected part name or index mismatch

preconditions: Wasp_Basic Part components already defined with named parts
Wasp_Connection From Direction used to define connections on each part (providing 0-based indices)
Part names used in P1/P2 exactly match the NAME input on corresponding Wasp_Basic Part components
Integer sliders or panels prepared for C1/C2 inputs referencing valid connection indices

evolution_history.changes: The new pattern confirms WaspRule objects are a required pipeline prerequisite for the aggregation component, clarifying the downstream role of rules in the assembly growth process.
